thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the desk,
the bell.

Go outside.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is an address. Works out where it is along the row, remembers it as my place, and tells my cottage to stand there.

team.name: Move when the bell rings
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest -- the bell. Sends [the ding, where I live, my own bird] to the desk and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

thing.name: Next address
thing.note: Problem 1, answered: guest i lives at cottage i. Takes the [number, bird] letter off the post and gives the bird a copy of the number.

thing.name: Move up five
thing.note: Problem 2, answered: everybody moves up five, which empties cottages 1 to 5 for the newcomers. Takes the [ding, where I live, bird] letter off the post, adds 5, and gives the answer to the bird.

thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

You are the clerk. Guests
arrive; every guest needs a
cottage, and no two cottages
may stand at the same address.

Each cottage has robots of
its own (inside the pad "the
guests"): it asks the desk
where to live, and stands
there. You never need to
touch those.

What is yours is the
arithmetic: a robot at the
desk that says WHERE, and
later one that says WHERE TO
MOVE.

Set the Speed to 4x or 8x: a
resort takes a while at
walking pace.

PROBLEM 1
The first infinite group

Six guests are at the gate,
numbered 1 to 6, and more are
behind them for ever.

On the grass is the desk: a box
holding one nest, THE POST.
Every guest writes to it.

Train a robot on that box to
take the [number, bird] letter
off the post and give the bird
the address. Give the box to
your robot and press Start:
with the nest empty it dozes,
which is what a clerk does.

Then press SPACE on the pad
"the guests": they ask, and
they house themselves.

Where should guest 1 live?
("Next address", on the grass,
is one answer.)

PROBLEM 2
Five more, and no room

Five more guests arrive, and
every cottage is taken. You
cannot turn them away: this is
Resort Infinity.

A guest asking to MOVE writes a
longer letter: [ding | where I
live | my bird]. Train a second
robot for that letter — five
further along — and drop it on
your first robot. They are a
team now, and a team runs
whichever member fits the
letter on top. Start it again.

Ring the bell: drop a ding on
the bell bird, and watch the
row shuffle up.

When cottages 1 to 5 stand
empty, press SPACE on "five
more guests".

Everybody moved; nobody was
turned out; nobody shares an
address. Why does that work
here and not at a hotel with a
hundred rooms?

THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages is what fits
on this grass. The row does
not stop at the fence: guest
12 stands past it, and guest
a thousand a long way past.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.
